ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended) for Yuhan Hoesa formation; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Act No. 8635, as amended), its Presidential Enforcement Decree and FSC Regulations for licensed securities brokerage, customer protection and AML; Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree for AML reporting and beneficial owner disclosure; Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee Act (Act No. 5493, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 5550, as amended); and the FSC and KoFIU Regulations on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporation Registration (Corporate Registry Extract) - Beob-in Deunggi-sa-hang Jeungmyeongseo
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registry Office of the Korean Supreme Court through the Internet Registration Office (or equivalent foreign corporate registrar for foreign applicant entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarize the certificate in the country of origin, then obtain a single apostille from the designated central authority of an Apostille Convention state (for Korea, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs). For a non-member state, obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate after authentication by the foreign ministry. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Clearance Certificate - Napse-jeungmyeongseo
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (or the competent foreign tax authority for foreign entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the central authority of the state where the tax certificate is issued (for Korea, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member. If the issuing state is not a member, consular legalization by the Korean mission with jurisdiction. Only one of these two authentication methods is used for each document; they never run in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation Acts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the applicant entity or the notary office of the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The document is notarized in the issuing jurisdiction. For an Apostille Convention state, the notarized document receives one apostille from the competent central authority. For a non-member state, the document receives consular legalization from the Korean consular post after local foreign ministry authentication. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes and are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and a notary public in the jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After notarization, an apostille must be affixed by the competent authority of the country of formation if that country is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. If the country is not a party, the Korean consular post must perform consular legalization. The two paths are mutually exclusive and cannot be applied to the same document in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter or Provisional Account Deposit Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the account or issuing the reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank document must be notarized and then either apostilled by the central authority of an Apostille Convention state or, for non-member states, legalized by the Korean consulate after foreign office authentication. No document should receive both an apostille and consular legalization; the appropriate path is chosen solely by the membership status of the issuing state.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any engagement, the applicant entity, its shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, agents and counterparties must be screened against the Korean consolidated sanctions list administered by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the U.S. OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the UK sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any foreign or domestic PEP, international organization PEP, family members and close associates, including verified source of wealth and source of funds. Screening is repeated at onboarding, at every client or transaction trigger, and after each sanctions list addition or amendment. Audit trail evidence must be retained in accordance with the Financial Transaction Reports Act for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in the Korean national script and include the suffix Yuhan Hoesa for a limited liability company, together with a transliterated trade name in Latin script for international filings. The Korean script name is controlling over any English phonetic transliteration. The name must be distinct from existing registered trade names in the same registry, must not mislead as to governmental or financial regulatory connection, and must follow the four-tier naming convention: (1) trade name; (2) business purpose; (3) Yuhan Hoesa legal-form suffix; and (4) registered office location and branch identifiers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Supreme Court registry rejects a proposed Yuhan Hoesa name, the applicant should first obtain a written rejection grounds notice from the registry officer. Under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, the applicant or counsel may file an immediate appeal with the competent District Court within two weeks of notification. The appeal must include the initial name-search result, the proposed correction, authenticated identity and authorization documents, a legal opinion on non-infringement and non-confusion with existing registered names, and the regulatory license plan for the securities brokerage purpose. A favorable court decision ordering registration is the binding remedy; administrative reconsideration through the registry superior office may be attempted but does not suspend statutory deadlines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in offshore securities brokerage, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the licensed registered office. The Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act requires a licensed financial investment business entity to maintain a physical office in Korea, with segregated client asset accounts, an AML compliance program, record-keeping systems and responsible personnel available during ordinary business hours. The National Tax Service and the registry also expect an actual leased address, and the Financial Services Commission will not treat a virtual office as an acceptable place of business. A virtual address may be used only as a supplementary service address and never for regulatory registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections by municipal tax officers and FSC/KoFIU examiners are highly likely; quantified risk is 85 percent within the first 12 months after licensing. The inspection checklist includes proof of lease and utility use, presence of a resident director or compliance officer, employee attendance records, business logs and server systems, segregated client asset ledger, AML risk assessment and internal controls, Board resolutions and financial records. Failure to pass a physical inspection may subject the entity to license revocation and administrative fines.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, 1962, as amended), notably Articles 292, 295, 301, 312, 313, 317, 318, 335, 388, 393, 397, 399, 401 and 402; together with the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Act No. 8636, 2007, as amended), Articles 12, 14, 24, 25, 28 and 303, and the Enforcement Decree and Regulations of the Financial Services Commission promulgated thereunder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court exercising territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (BEOPINDEUNG-GI SINCHUNG SEO) and the notarized Articles of Incorporation therewith filed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Commercial Act of Korea, a Yuhan Hoesa has no statutory minimum paid-up capital. However, because the entity will operate as a licensed investment brokerage under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, the Financial Services Commission prescribes a minimum initial paid-up capital of KRW 5,000,000,000 for retail securities brokerage, or any higher amount set by the FSC at the time of application. This capital must be fully paid before the FSC license is issued and must be maintained in a blocked escrow deposit account at a domestic bank; a balance confirmation certificate issued by the bank must be attached to both the court incorporation registration and the FSC license application. The escrow funds cannot be released until the incorporation registration has been completed and the FSC license has been approved, except as expressly permitted under insolvency or statutory void-ab-initio rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA)

I, [NAME], acting as sole incorporator and sole initial director of the Company, in accordance with the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Company's notarized Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopt the following resolutions:

1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL: The authorized initial paid-up capital of the Company is fully subscribed by the subscriber named in the Articles of Incorporation, who shall pay the subscription price in cash into the Company's capital escrow account at [BANK NAME] in the Republic of Korea. The Board authorizes the depositary bank to issue a balance certificate to the Commercial Registry. No subscription money shall be returned before completion of the incorporation registration, except under narrowly-defined statutory exclusions.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The following individuals are hereby appointed as signatories for all corporate banking relationships: [Representative Director] and [Chief Financial Officer]. Co-signatory authority is established for any transaction in excess of KRW [AMOUNT], and the bank mandate shall permit the opening of segregated client money accounts, settlement accounts, tax payment accounts and operating accounts. The signatories are authorized to execute account opening forms, mandates, electronic banking control forms, fraud-prevention acknowledgements and collateral or depository agreements consistent with the regulatory license.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company is adopted as [FULL ADDRESS], Seoul, Republic of Korea, and the registered agent named in the Articles is authorized to accept service of process and governmental notices. The registered office must be continuously maintained, and any relocation shall be registered promptly as a material amendment.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The following statutory officers are appointed to hold office until the first annual general meeting of shareholders: [NAME], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [NAME], Chief Financial Officer; [NAME], Chief Compliance Officer; [NAME], Anti-Money Laundering Officer; and [NAME], Statutory Auditor. Each officer accepts the appointment and shall discharge his or her duties of diligence and good faith in accordance with Article 382(3) and Article 399 of the Commercial Act.

5. EXECUTION OF REGULATORY ACTIONS: The Representative Director and the Chief Compliance Officer are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, sign, file and effect all regulatory filings, applications, registrations and notifications required for the Company's licensing, including electronic submissions to the court commercial registry, the National Tax Service, the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service, the Korea Financial Investment Association and the Korea Securities Depository. All authorizations shall remain valid until revoked by a subsequent written board resolution.

ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT this ___ day of ____________________, 20___.

[SIGNATURE] ____________________
[NAME]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of articles of incorporation, capital escrow and notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public under Article 292 of the Commercial Act, and the FSC-approved commercial bank branch selected by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address, business purpose of investment brokerage under ISIC 6611, share classes, authorized share capital, initial paid-up capital, board composition and statutory auditor provisions. Confirm that all subscriber identities pass the fit-and-proper screening and that no prohibited foreign shareholder restriction applies to the intended non-resident ownership. Submit signed copies to the notary public with the full identification dossier of every incorporating member and the original certified Korean translation of any foreign corporate resolutions. After notarization, open a temporary capital escrow account at a commercial bank in Korea and wire the full subscription amount. Obtain the bank-issued balance certificate in the name of the company to be formed in escrow. The notarized Articles must be executed and sealed within the statutory deadline and must remain materially unchanged before filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber identification documents
Power of attorney for agent filing, if applicable
Proof of domestic capital wire transfer
Temporary bank escrow account balance certificate
Consent forms for initial statutory officers
Draft business plan for retail securities brokerage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewer queries any capital or subscriber issue, cure the defect by correcting the articles and recertifying before the same notary, then resubmit. If the bank refuses to issue the escrow balance certificate, select an alternate FSC-listed bank and repeat the capital wiring and certificate issuance within the supplementary response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration at the commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court or the local District Court with territorial jurisdiction; online portal of the Supreme Court i-reg system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the competent court registry in the jurisdiction of the principal place of business. The application must contain the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital escrow balance certificate, appointment consents of directors and auditors, and the subscriber table. Verify every statutory particular against the court's public register, including corporate name, registered office, director names, shareholder details, paid-up capital and the date on which the corporate existence will attach. Pay the registration quota tax and court issuance fee, and obtain the certificate of corporate registration and corporate seal certificate. Under Articles 317 and 318 of the Commercial Act, registration must occur without delay after the company has been formed, and corporate legal personality takes effect upon the registration entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital escrow balance certificate
Court-prescribed incorporation registration application
Board minutes appointing representative director
Signed appointment consents of directors and auditor
Identification documents of all directors and auditor
Power of attorney if filed through a licensed attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for supplementation, complete all missing items within the court-specified period, normally no more than 30 calendar days. If the registration is rejected on substantive grounds, file an immediate appeal with the higher court against the rejection or re-file a fully corrected application after removing the stated defect; additional court fees will be billed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial investment business license approval from the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission; application intake through the Financial Supervisory Service specialized financial license window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a comprehensive authorization package for the financial investment business of investment brokerage under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. The application must show full compliance with FSC minimum paid-up capital rules, a permissible organizational structure, qualified executive officers, shareholder restructurings consistent with fit-and-proper standards, a compliance control system, a consumer protection policy, an anti-money laundering program, information security management system certificates, and a credible business plan addressing segregated client funds and cross-border brokerage operations. Attend the FSC deliberation committee interview if summoned. Once approved, the FSC issues a formal license naming the company and identifying the specific scope of investment brokerage; that license must be presented to the FSS before supervisory registration.
required_dossiers: FSC license application form
Corporate registration certificate and seal certificate
Bank certificate of fully paid initial capital
Detailed business plan for offshore retail brokerage
Organizational chart and governance manual
Compliance and AML internal control manuals
Shareholders list with beneficial ownership disclosures
Board resolution appointing compliance and AML officers
ISMS implementation certificate or security plan
Financial commitment evidence for capital adequacy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC issues a request for supplementary documentation, respond within 21 days with the full evidentiary record. If the FSC insists on rejecting the application, the company may file a reconsideration petition with the FSC within 15 days and thereafter challenge a final adverse determination in the Seoul Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-license onboarding with financial associations and settlement infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Service, Korea Financial Investment Association, Korea Securities Depository, and Korea Exchange or approved OTC infrastructure as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the FSC license certificate is issued, complete the FSS automatic administrative registration as a regulated financial institution, join the Korea Financial Investment Association, execute participant agreements with the Korea Securities Depository, and connect to the necessary trading or settlement systems if exchange-traded products are offered. Open segregated client money accounts at an FSC-approved domestic settlement bank and file a business commencement report with the FSS and the National Tax Service. Register dealing and investment advisory representatives, issue electronic authentication certificates for responsible officers, run parallel-system cycle tests with the settlement infrastructure, and publish the seat and contact information required under the Capital Markets Act.
required_dossiers: FSC license certificate
Corporate registration transcript and seal certificate
KOFIA membership application
KSD participant agreement and guarantee documents
Segregated client account opening certificates
Registered representative list and license filings
ISMS operation and disaster recovery plans
AML senior officer certification and external audit consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSS or KOFIA identifies onboarding deficiencies, file a corrective action plan with defined timelines and obtain written clearance from the compliance committee. If the settlement institution imposes enhanced monitoring conditions, address them through supplementary undertakings and internal risk procedures; unresolved disputes can be escalated to the institution's dispute review process or to the Financial Services Commission for supervisory direction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable -- this is an offshore securities brokerage operation with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing or physical industrial operation. The operative licensing authority is the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service for financial investment business licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Investment Business License (Investment Brokerage) under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable -- the Korean Ministry of Environment is not engaged because there is no physical facility, plant, land disturbance or discharge source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable -- pure financial office operation; no full EIA requirement, Environmental Registration tier or screening category applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable -- zero industrial wastewater, VOC or hazardous waste streams. The office operation is nevertheless obligated to dispose of used IT equipment through licensed e-waste recyclers under the Waste Management Act and to maintain ordinary office hygiene standards; there are no quantitative environmental thresholds applicable to this brokerage license.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial civil defense fire permits or warehouse fire approval, because no physical factory or storage facility is operated. As a standard office premises, the building owner must obtain the ordinary Fire Safety Inspection and Occupancy Certificate from the local fire station before occupancy. The company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by appointing a workplace safety manager, conducting emergency evacuation drills, maintaining extinguishers and clear exit paths, and recording workplace accident statistics. No additional chemical, structural or industrial civil defense clearance is required for this regulated financial services entity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); online portal: Home Tax Service (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Within 20 days after business commencement, the Yuhan Hoesa (domestic LLC) must file the business registration application with the local NTS tax office or through Hometax, attaching the court-certified corporate registration, articles of incorporation, and foreign investment notification certificate. NTS then issues the Business Registration Number (BRN) which functions as the VAT identification number. For foreign non-resident entities without a Korean establishment supplying VAT-liable services, registration is effected through a tax representative under the mandatory branch/land-based registration rules; the application is submitted with the foreign entity's home-country registration certificate, name and address details, and the designated Korean tax representative's identification. The tax representative must be a Korean resident or domestic corporation authorized to receive NTS notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; a domestic company is classified by statute as a general corporation taxed at entity level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration from the first business supply (no turnover threshold); simplified taxpayer scheme for small businesses with annual revenue not exceeding 80,000,000 KRW (as adjusted by law).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every VAT-registered business must issue a Korean electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) through the NTS Home Tax Service electronic invoicing system; invoice data must be transmitted to NTS within 1 day after issuing the invoice. There is no separate real-time fiscal clearance stamp, but the NTS electronic invoice matching system validates transmitted data against compliance criteria and flags anomalies. Anti-fraud digital stamping is integrated into the NTS e-invoice platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exported goods and to services supplied to a non-resident where the service is either performed outside Korea or is confirmed as consumed outside Korea. For offshore securities brokerage, the commission/service fee is zero-rated when the client is a non-resident, the execution of the trade is confirmed abroad, and the service shows evident overseas consumption; the brokerage contract and order records must evidence the overseas supply. Otherwise, financial brokerage services are VAT-exempt if performed in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Cargo Documents)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing export from Korea
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean bank confirming repatriation of export proceeds
Signed offshore brokerage contract, overseas client identification files, and execution confirmations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS cross-validates export declarations with customs manifest data and bank foreign-exchange remittance certificates. Zero-rated sales lacking the required documentation or remittance proof are recharged with 10% VAT plus penalty tax; fraudulent claims attract added penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes (up to 40% of avoided VAT) and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank, with foreign exchange administration jointly exercised through the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and BOK Foreign Exchange Trading Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised current-account and capital-account regime for the Korean won. The won is convertible at market rates through authorised foreign exchange banks for trade, service, investment, and treasury transactions. Current-account payments do not require prior exchange control approval, but every foreign-exchange transaction should be supported by an underlying document and reported to the Bank of Korea as part of balance-of-payments statistics. Capital-account transactions operate under a negative-list approach: inward foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, overseas investment, and financial derivatives generally require reporting or prior approval depending on category and size. Profit repatriation via dividends is freely permitted after tax clearance and audit certification, but the handling bank will require audited financial statements, board resolution, tax payment receipts, and a purpose code. The practical hurdle for a high-risk offshore securities brokerage is not exchange control prohibition, but documentation completeness and bank de-risking. The BOK may impose macro-prudential measures, such as aggregate foreign-exchange derivative position limits, which indirectly affect hedging availability. FATCA/CRS confirmation and anti-tax-avoidance declarations remain unavoidable. Overall, there is no material convertibility restriction on legitimate commercial flows, but the foreign-exchange bank has full compliance discretion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related BOK enforcement rules, resident exporters must collect export proceeds within four months from the date of the export declaration. The handling foreign exchange bank can grant an extension of up to two months when justifiable circumstances such as documentary discrepancies are evidenced, and the extension is reported to the Bank of Korea. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; exporters may keep the foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account at an authorised bank or convert it into KRW at market rates. All export proceeds must nevertheless be received through a licensed foreign exchange bank and cannot be settled through offshore EMIs or unlicensed payment intermediaries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Current Account
Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Current Account
Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account and KRW Basic Operational Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Non-Viable for any standalone bank-like onboarding. South Korean law only recognises foreign exchange banks authorised under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for FX settlement, corporate deposits, and SWIFT clearing. Offshore digital EMI providers have no legal ability to open KRW accounts for a Korean entity, issue local IBAN numbers, or perform capital verification. A fintech that holds an Electronic Financial Transactions Act licence may act only as an electronic payment/prepaid service in KRW, not as a corporate treasury clearing bank. For this high-risk securities brokerage, a Korean Tier-1 commercial bank is mandatory for compliant segregated client wiring and FX.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. For a foreign-controlled, high-risk securities brokerage, banks require at least one statutory director or a fully authorised senior signatory to appear in person at the domestic branch to sign account mandates and complete customer identification. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as the sole path; however, after notarisation and apostille/consular legalisation of a power of attorney, the bank may allow the appointed representative to finalise the account, subject to a high-assurance video interview and direct verification of the corporate registry records at the source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity created by multiple Korean and offshore holding layers, nominee shareholdings or trust arrangements; the bank cannot identify the natural person controlling the securities brokerage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled group ownership chart down to each natural person over the 25% threshold; full registered shareholder list; overseas corporate registry extracts; trust documents or nominee declarations; passport and tax identification for each UBO; sworn statement describing source of shares and economic rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk product line in retail equities, CFDs and derivatives without clear Korean Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act authorisation; bank compliance cannot confirm whether the brokerage is legally licensed to solicit Korean or cross-border clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified home-regulator licence; FSCMA legal opinion from a Korean attorney; registration certificate showing ISIC 6611 / NAICS 523120 scope; audited financial statements for two years; AML programme narrative, transaction monitoring rules, client suitability policy; proof of regulatory communications and criminal/police vetting for directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unstructured high-volume third-party client wires into one segregated omnibus account, representing layering and fungibility risks; the bank cannot attribute each wire to a verifiable investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated client sub-ledger showing beneficiary interest; sample SWIFT MT103 logs with unique purpose codes and full originator information; bank BIC and jurisdiction list for counterparties; FATCA/CRS registration; independent auditor opinion on client money controls; transaction-monitoring exception report for the first 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons exposure in the distribution map; any hint of clients from OFAC/EU/UN sanctioned jurisdictions or high-risk counterparties will cause a referral to the bank's sanctions committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified IP geo-blocking configuration that prevents onboarding in prohibited jurisdictions; PEP screening output with no adverse matches; adverse-media due diligence for every beneficial owner; signing officer compliance letter stating geo-blocking is active; prohibition of services to anonymous wallets; periodic sanctions testing report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be routed as a SWIFT MT103/MT202 corporate wire from the shareholder's bank to the Company's foreign currency account at the designated Korean foreign exchange bank. The remittance must be accompanied by a foreign exchange purpose code and underlying foreign direct investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The handling bank issues a foreign investment registration certificate after verifying the remittance and filing with the Ministry of Economy and Finance/Bank of Korea. For paid-in capital, a certified public accountant in Korea performs capital verification and issues a Korean capital verification report confirming the KRW/USD conversion rate, FX calculation, and deposit into the domestic account. No funds may be accepted through cryptocurrency, client-to-client, or unlicensed EMI channels for capital formation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Client cash withdrawals and operational trade disbursements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 over the Tier-1 bank's overseas correspondent network. For interbank treasury funding, hedge collateral and custody settlement, SWIFT MT202/MT202COV should be used to ensure cover payment transparency; MT100/MT199 messages are not sufficient. For physical treasury transactions with commodities, a Commercial LC (MT700) or Documentary Collection (MT400) can be issued through the same licensed bank, but the standard retail securities brokerage flow should rely on segregated custody clearing rather than trade documentary collection. All outbound payments must be declared with the proper BOK purpose code and accompanied by contract, invoice or board instruction so the bank can complete post-transaction reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with documented underlying trade, dividend or investment exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through an authorised foreign exchange bank with non-resident counterparties and explicit real-demand documentation
Cross-currency swaps for asset-liability management of foreign exchange capital or borrowed funds
FX options combined with forwards for hedge-only purposes; naked speculative options are not permitted without a financial investment licence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members: approval of annual financial statements and appointment or continuation of the external certified auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the Yuhan Hoesa (LLC); minutes recorded in the statutory corporate minute book; no government filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 against responsible managers or members; judicial convocation at company expense upon member application; repeated failure to hold the meeting may support a court order for dissolution; for a licensed securities broker, such failure constitutes a regulatory licensing deficiency that can lead to FSC administrative sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and final tax settlement for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% for underreporting, 10% for non-payment, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% on unpaid corporate tax; seizure and forced collection by the National Tax Service; criminal referral for intentional tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual external audit report and audited financial statements under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service and Financial Services Commission electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent CPA audit must be completed and the auditor's report presented to members with the ordinary general meeting; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the audited financial statements must be delivered to the supervisory authority on or before 31 March, with the customary FSS submission within 14 days after member receipt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to KRW 30,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years for failure to appoint an external auditor or to file audited financial statements; administrative monetary sanctions, suspension or revocation of the securities brokerage licence; FSC strike-off from the financial investment business register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report (business year report) of the financial investment business entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service DART electronic disclosure system, and Korea Financial Investment Association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, on or before 31 March; material facts reports due within 15 days of reportable events
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 50,000,000; corrective order; public censure; suspension or revocation of brokerage licence; wilful non-disclosure creates criminal liability and can support administrative strike-off from the financial services register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT independent audit, beneficial ownership confirmation, and compliance report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual independent AML audit and Board-approved compliance confirmation must be completed before the ordinary general meeting; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, due by 31 March; suspicious transaction reports remain due within 3 days throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 100,000,000; corrective orders; criminal fines and imprisonment under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Information; loss of segregated client wire acceptance privileges and termination of payment network access.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of foreign-invested status and transfer reporting for non-resident membership interests
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit where UBO changes are involved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any acquisition or transfer of 10% or more of membership units or any change in controlling beneficial ownership; annual UBO confirmation must also be completed and filed in the register of members before the ordinary general meeting (31 March for a calendar year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years for failure to report foreign investment changes; suspension of voting rights for non-compliant transfers; AML penalties for late or false UBO information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory when the company's total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end. In addition, a licensed financial investment business entity, including a retail securities brokerage for equities, CFDs and derivatives, is always subject to compulsory external audit irrespective of asset size. The Korean external audit framework does not use annual turnover or headcount as separate stand-alone audit triggers; however, a regulated brokerage house is captured unconditionally through its FSC financial investment business licence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for all licensed financial investment business entities and public-interest corporations; K-GAAP (Korean GAAP) is permitted only for non-listed non-financial SMEs that are not otherwise required to apply K-IFRS; securities brokerage financial statements must follow K-IFRS plus FSC supervisory reporting formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current register of members identifying each member's legal name, residential or registered address, number of membership units, acquisition date, and transfer history. Any non-resident acquisition or transfer of 10% or more of total membership units must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days. For AML purposes, the ultimate beneficial owner of every client relationship and every member with 10% or greater ownership must be identified and re-verified annually before the ordinary general meeting; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed with KoFIU within 30 days. There is no single central Korean UBO registry for domestic LLCs, but the internal UBO register is a mandatory on-site statutory and AML record and must be available for inspection by the FSS, KoFIU, and the National Tax Service.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges or Mortgages over Company Assets
Register of Pledges and Encumbrances over Membership Units
Minute Book of General Meetings of Members and Management Meetings
Statutory Accounting Books and Supporting Voucher Files
AML/CFT Beneficial Ownership Register and High-Risk Client Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 per annum for a licensed corporate secretarial agent and registered-office package in Seoul; USD 8,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a physical business-district office suitable for a regulated brokerage operation.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 45,000 per annum for a certified CPA audit of a licensed retail securities brokerage with segregated client funds, multi-currency settlement, CFD and derivative transactions, and mandatory AML/CFT audit procedures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top statutory bracket for taxable income above KRW 20 billion plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, producing a 24.2% aggregate top headline rate; lower brackets are 9% and 19%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box applies to an ISIC 6611 securities brokerage license. Korea offers targeted corporate tax reductions for foreign-invested businesses in free economic zones (100% reduction for three years followed by 50% for two years), R&D tax credits up to 25-30%, tax credit for job-creating capital investment, and foreign tax credit relief for income already taxed abroad under a bilateral treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Corporate Income Tax Return) e-filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal, together with Financial Statements, related-party transaction schedules, and the Foreign Tax Credit computation form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa the final return is due by March 31 of the following year, with extensions available under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, ownership structure, and business license details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean taxpayer registration number, foreign shareholder percentages, and the offshore securities brokerage license number. For a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa, attach the definitive ownership schedule and tax representative appointment certificate to avoid penalties for undisclosed foreign ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total domestic and foreign-source brokerage revenue, including commission, spreads, and CFD or derivative transaction income arising from retail agency activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Korean-source brokerage income gross without netting out distribution or clearing fees. Segregate fees from foreign clients booked through the Korean permanent establishment, and identify intercompany service invoices using the transaction codes required by the International Tax Adjustment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for management fees, IT services, order-execution services, risk management services, and software royalties paid to affiliated offshore entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only where arm's length pricing is substantiated and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation exists. For non-resident payees, identify the applicable DTA article and confirm that withholding was applied to any Korean-source royalty or technical service fee; a missing beneficial ownership declaration will invalidate the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after carryforward loss deduction, prior-year adjustments, special tax credits, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should verify that the tax base here is the same base used for branch profit tax if the Yuhan Hoesa is treated as a Korean permanent establishment of a foreign securities group. Attach the statutory loss carryforward schedule (maximum 10 years) and reconcile any audit adjustments against the financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge calculated at 10% of national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief does not automatically excuse the local surtax; the relevant DTA must be expressly claimed on the return. If the surtax is assessed on foreign-source income that was already subject to foreign tax, attach the foreign tax credit schedule to prevent double taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional penalty of 20% of the unpaid national tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes; negligent under-reporting adds 10%; fraudulent non-reporting or excessive refund claims add 40%. Overdue tax accrues daily late-payment interest at the annual statutory rate (effectively about 0.025% per day, compounded). Failure to file the related-party transaction schedule adds a 20% documentation penalty. Criminal tax evasion through false brokerage books is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and carries imprisonment up to five years and/or a fine up to KRW 100 million, with increased sanctions for evasion exceeding KRW 500 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding on outbound cash and deemed dividends paid by a Korean corporation to non-resident shareholders, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the withholding, producing a 22% aggregate domestic rate. A Korean permanent establishment remitting branch profits after tax is additionally exposed to a 22% branch profits tax, as applicable under the Corporate Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim bilateral DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the resident jurisdiction; (2) submit the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Korean withholding agent before dividend remittance; (3) file the tax treaty exemption/reduction application through HomeTax together with the withholding return; (4) maintain board minutes, share register, and evidence demonstrating substantive business purpose and real investment substance to defeat the Korean conduit-company doctrine; and (5) if withholding was applied at the statutory rate, file a timely correction claim within the generally applicable five-year limitation period to recover the excess withheld tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and intercompany interest is 20% plus 2% local surtax (22% aggregate). Under most Korean bilateral DTA agreements, royalties are reduced to 10% for industrial/commercial payments and 15% for certain cultural rights, while interest is generally reduced to 10% or 14% in older treaties, conditional on beneficial ownership and absence of anti-conduit abuse.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; Country-by-Country Reporting is triggered at KRW 100 billion consolidated group turnover. The National Tax Service may nonetheless require contemporaneous documentation below these thresholds for offshore brokerage structures bearing treaty, conduit, or captive-intermediary indicia.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a substance-over-form and beneficial-ownership anti-avoidance doctrine under the Income Tax Act, the Corporate Tax Act, and the International Tax Adjustment Act. Although Korea is not a Crown Dependency subject to the OECD ESR template, an offshore securities brokerage Yuhan Hoesa must prove Core Income-Generating Activities including client contracting, order execution, trade booking, risk management, valuation, and compliance oversight. A shell entity lacking local employees and decision-making control will be denied treaty benefits, its income re-attributed to the non-resident principal, and its intercompany fees recharacterised as constructive dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of retail commission income from offshore equity, CFD, and derivative transactions using shadow ledgers and fabricated client-payment reversal entries, combined with false deductible expenses in the brokerage revenue schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act additional taxes of 40% of evaded national tax plus 10% local surtax penalty; Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) imposes imprisonment not exceeding five years and/or a fine not exceeding KRW 100 million, increased for evasion of KRW 500 million or more.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where directors engaged in intentional concealment; directors are jointly and severally liable to the National Tax Service for the unpaid tax, penalty surcharges, and interest. The director becomes a delinquent taxpayer subject to travel ban and passport invalidation, and criminally liable to imprisonment up to seven years with court-ordered restitution of the hidden profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell Conduit Entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking all brokerage margin and risk reward to a related offshore entity without a local office, staff, board meetings, or independent risk decisions; failing to file the related-party transaction schedule and contemporaneous Local File despite exceeding the KRW 10 billion threshold; paying inflated intercompany technology and management fees to strip Korean taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 5 permit the National Tax Service to recompute taxable income on an arm's length basis; Article 26 penalises failure to submit transfer pricing documents by up to 30% of the adjusted tax amount; the Framework Act under-reporting penalty adds 40% for fraudulent transfer-pricing concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute sham pricing are personally liable under the Korean Commercial Act for damages to creditors and the tax authority; personal assets may be attached for the tax deficit, the director is disqualified from managing any regulated Korean financial company, and a criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can impose imprisonment or a fine when the arrangement is a cloak for concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Securities Brokerage and AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating retail securities brokerage under ISIC 6611 without a Financial Services Commission license under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA), and accepting client funds through segregated wires and card rails without implementing mandatory anti-money-laundering controls required by the Reporting and Use of Financial Transaction Information Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FSCMA Articles 44 and 448 impose imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to KRW 200 million for unregistered financial investment business; the AML Act separately penalises failure to report suspicious transactions and can result in asset freezes, corrective orders, and licence revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the unlicensed brokerage are jointly and severally liable for client losses, subject to travel bans and passport invalidation, and criminally liable to imprisonment up to five years; foreign directors can be prosecuted in absentia with enforcement pursued through mutual legal assistance and extradition channels.
